source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension (នាយកដ្ឋានផ្សព្វផ្សាយកសិកម្ម) - "ដំណាំក្រូចពោធិសាត់" (Pursat Orange Cultivation Guide), 2016, 26pp
text:
Once a suitable site has been chosen and the soil assessed, farmers dig planting holes and space the trees to allow good growth and easy orchard management. Before digging, it helps to mark out planting rows and hole positions evenly across the plot.

Compost or well-rotted manure is commonly mixed into the soil that will be used to backfill each planting hole, to give young trees a nutrient-rich start. Grafted or marcotted planting stock is transplanted from its nursery container into the prepared hole, taking care not to bury the graft union below the soil line. Planting is best timed for the rainy season, when natural rainfall reduces the need for manual watering while the tree establishes.
